raw_text:
Here’s the complete 12-week prenatal plan summary, integrating strength, pressing focus, higher-intent Phase 2, core, cardio, nutrition, and Week 12 “peak feel” guidelines. Designed for an advanced lifter at 20–32 weeks, cleared for moderate strength; avoids supine after 16 weeks, no max attempts, no Valsalva, symptom-aware at all times.

Global structure and guardrails
- Weekly schedule: 3 strength days (Mon lower, Wed upper, Fri full-body) + 2 cardio sessions + optional short recovery cardio. Add 10–15 minutes of core at the end of each lift.
- Intensity anchors: Ph1 RPE 6–7; Ph2 RPE 7.5–8 on primaries; Ph3 RPE 6–7. Leave 2–3 reps in reserve; no grinders.
- Movement positions: Prioritize standing, seated, side-lying, incline (20–45°), half/tall-kneeling. No flat supine.
- Bracing/breathing: 360° inhale, gentle brace, exhale on exertion; no breath holding.
- Red flags to stop/modify: dizziness, chest pain, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, unusual SOB, calf pain/swelling, pronounced pelvic pain/pressure, or midline coning.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and volume (RPE 6–7)
- Goal: Solid movement quality, posture, pelvic floor connection, moderate loads.

Week 1
- Day 1 Lower: SSB or goblet squat 4x6; RDL 3x8; split squat 3x8/side; pull-through 3x10; side-lying Pallof 3x10/side
- Day 2 Upper (press emphasis): Incline DB press 4x8; 1-arm cable row 4x8/side; landmine press 3x10; pulldown 3x10; face pulls 3x12
- Day 3 Full: Trap bar DL 4x5; FFE split squat 3x8/side; seated row 3x10; chest-supported DB row/raise 2x12; tall-kneeling chop 3x10/side
- Core (add post-session): Connection breath; side-lying Pallof; tall-kneeling anti-extension; bird dog (short lever)
- Cardio: 2 sessions—25–30 min steady (RPE 5–6) and 3–5 x 2 min @ RPE 6–7 with 2 min easy
- Nutrition highlights: +250–450 kcal/day above maintenance; protein 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; carbs 3–5 g/kg/day; prenatal micronutrients; hydrate 2.5–3.0 L/day

Week 2
- Day 1: SSB squat 4x6–7; RDL 3x8–9; walking lunge 3x10/side; elevated hip thrust 3x10; side plank (knees) w/ row 3x20–30s
- Day 2: Incline DB press 4x8–9; chest-supported row 4x8; half-kneeling landmine press 3x8/side; pulldown 3x8–10; Y-T-W 2x12; suitcase hold 3x30–40s/side
- Day 3: Trap bar DL 4x5–6; step-up 3x8/side; pull-through 3x12; incline machine press 3x10; Pallof 3x12/side
- Core: Half-kneeling anti-rotation; tall-kneeling lift; side plank short lever; quadruped heel slides
- Cardio: Repeat W1, progress minutes slightly if RPE allows

Week 3
- Day 1: Front squat w/ straps or SSB 4x5–6; RDL 3x8; reverse lunge 3x8/side; hip abduction 3x12; clamshell 2x15/side
- Day 2 (press heavy feel): Incline barbell press 4x6; 1-arm DB row 4x8/side; strict landmine press 3x8; neutral pulldown 3x10; face pulls 3x12
- Day 3: Trap bar DL 4x4–5; Bulgarian split squat 3x8/side; seated row 3x10; anti-extension pulldown 3x12; incline lateral raises 2x12
- Core: Incline dead bug; half-kneeling Pallof to overhead; slow anti-extension; farmer march
- Cardio: As W2

Week 4 (slight deload if needed)
- Day 1: SSB squat 3x5–6; elevated hip thrust 3x8; step-downs 2x10/side; pull-through 2x12
- Day 2: Incline DB press 3x8; chest-supported row 3x8; landmine press 3x8; pulldown 2x10; face pulls 2x12
- Day 3: Trap bar DL 3x4–5; split squat 2x8/side; seated row 2x10; Pallof 2x12/side
- Core: Side-lying downtraining breaths; tall-kneeling chop; side plank w/ row; bird dog + light band
- Cardio: Steady 25–30 min + optional 15–20 min easy flush

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength emphasis with higher intent (RPE 7.5–8 on primaries)
- Changes: Top set + back-offs, clusters, density; tighter rest on accessories. Cardio includes sharper but submax intervals.

Week 5
- Day 1 Lower: SSB box squat top 1x4 @ RPE 8 + back-off 3x4 @ RPE 7–7.5; RDL 4x6 @ RPE 7.5; heavy sled push 6–8 x 20–25 m; walking lunge 2x12/side
- Day 2 Upper (press priority): Incline barbell press top 1x5 @ RPE 8 + 3x5 @ RPE 7–7.5; chest-supported 1-arm row 4x8/side @ RPE 8; landmine press clusters 3x(6+3)/side; neutral pulldown 3x8; finisher 6-min density—incline DB press (8) + serratus punch (12)
- Day 3 Full: Trap bar DL 5x3 @ RPE 8; FFE split squat 3x8/side; 10-min EDT—seated row (8) + incline machine press (8)
- Core: Tall-kneeling anti-extension 4x8; half-kneeling Pallof 3x10/side; landmine anti-rotation 3x8/side; heavy suitcase carry 3x50–60 m/side
- Cardio: 30–35 min steady + intervals 8–10 x 60s @ RPE 7 w/ 60–90s easy
- Fueling: Pre 40–70 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; consider intra 15–30 g carbs if sessions >70 min

Week 6
- Day 1: SSB box squat 5x4 @ RPE 7.5–8; RDL 4x6 @ RPE 8; sled 6–8 x 25–30 m; elevated hip thrust 3x8 @ RPE 8

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week + 1 optional low-impact conditioning/mobility day
- Session length: 45–70 minutes (including warm-up and cool-down)
- Intensity: Mostly RPE 6–8 or 60–75% e1RM; avoid grinding reps; leave 2–4 reps in reserve (RIR)
- Core and floor: Emphasize pelvic floor and deep core in warm-up and accessories; avoid high intra-abdominal pressure and traditional supine crunches/sit-ups; prefer side-lying, quadruped, tall/half-kneeling, incline, or standing
- Breathing and bracing: Exhale on exertion; no Valsalva. Use 360° breathing and submax bracing
- Supine modification: Replace flat back-lying after week 16 with 30–45° incline or side-lying

Phases

- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Strength emphasis with controlled intensity (RPE 7–8), maintain submax; adjust ROM as needed

Cool-down (5–8 min)

Here’s a pragmatic prenatal nutrition plan to support a 30-year-old advanced lifter at ~20–32 weeks, aiming to maintain lean mass, fuel training, and meet pregnancy needs. Coordinate specifics with her OB/midwife and a registered dietitian, especially for weight-gain targets and supplements.

Goals and guardrails
- Primary: Support fetal development, adequate weight gain, and maternal health.
- Secondary: Maintain lean mass and strength performance.
- Approach: High-protein, fiber-rich, micronutrient-dense diet with steady carbs around training, adequate fats, and smart hydration/electrolytes.

Energy and weight gain
- Trimester 2–3 energy: +250–450 kcal/day above pre-pregnancy maintenance, adjusted to:
  - Rate of gain per OB guidance (commonly ~0.3–0.5 kg/week in T2/T3 for normal BMI; individualize for starting BMI).
  - Training days: aim the higher end of the range; rest days: lower end.
- Practical check-ins: If energy flags in workouts, hunger between meals rises, morning weight trends flat for 2–3 weeks, or recovery worsens, add ~150–200 kcal/day.

Macronutrients
- Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day (up to 2.0 g/kg if well tolerated), spread over 4–5 feedings.
  - Target 25–40 g high-quality protein per meal; 20–30 g per snack.
  - Include leucine-rich sources to support MPS: dairy, eggs, lean meat, whey/Greek yogurt, soy.
- Carbohydrates: 3–5 g/kg/day as baseline, flexing up on hard training days.
  - Emphasize complex carbs and fiber (oats, rice, potatoes, legumes, fruit, whole grains).
  - Pre/post-training carbs prioritized; keep steady carbs across the day to manage energy and nausea.
- Fats: 25–35% of calories.
  - Focus on mono- and polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, fatty fish within mercury guidance).
  - Include omega-3s (DHA/EPA).

Meal timing around training
- 60–120 min pre-workout: 40–70 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; low-moderate fat, low spice to reduce reflux.
  - Examples: Greek yogurt + granola + berries; turkey sandwich on whole grain; rice + eggs.
- During: For sessions >75 min or in heat, sip water; consider 15–30 g easily digested carbs if energy dips.
- Post-workout (within 1–2 hours): 30–40 g protein + 60–90 g carbs.
  - Examples: whey + banana + oats; rice bowl with salmon/chicken + veggies.
- Bedtime snack (optional): 20–30 g protein (casein/Greek yogurt/cottage cheese) + fiber/healthy fat to support satiety and overnight recovery.

Hydration and electrolytes
- Fluids: ~2.5–3.0 L/day baseline, plus 500–750 ml per training hour and more in heat.
- Electrolytes: Add 300–600 mg sodium during long/hot sessions; include potassium and magnesium from foods (bananas, potatoes, leafy greens, nuts). Choose low- or no-caffeine options later in the day.

Micronutrient priorities
- Prenatal vitamin: Daily, covering folate (as methylfolate if indicated), iodine (~150 mcg), iron, choline, vitamin D, B12. Verify doses with provider.
- Iron: Screen levels; if low or vegetarian, supplement per provider. Pair iron foods with vitamin C for absorption; separate from calcium and coffee/tea by 1–2 hours.
- Choline: ~450 mg/day (eggs, lean meats, soy, supplementation if intake is low).
- DHA/EPA: ~300–500 mg DHA/day. Use low-mercury fish (salmon, sardines) 2x/week or an algal/fish oil supplement.
- Calcium: ~1,000 mg/day from dairy/fortified alternatives/leafy greens; if supplementing, split doses.
- Vitamin D: Test and supplement to achieve sufficiency (often 1,000–2,000 IU/day; provider-guided).
- Iodine: Ensure via prenatal and iodized salt unless contraindicated.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day from whole foods to support GI health; increase fluids concurrently.

Food safety and pregnancy-specific guidance
- Avoid high-mercury fish (shark, swordfish, king mackerel, tilefish); limit albacore tuna.
- No unpasteurized dairy/juices, undercooked meats/eggs, or deli meats unless reheated steaming hot.
- Wash produce thoroughly; practice safe food handling.
- Caffeine: ≤200 mg/day total.
- Manage reflux and nausea: smaller, more frequent meals; avoid large/fatty/spicy meals close to bed; elevate head of bed if needed.

Sample day (approx. 2,300–2,600 kcal; 160–180 g protein; adjust portions to body size)
- Breakfast: Greek yogurt parfait with 1 cup Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup granola, mixed berries, chia; 1 boiled egg.
- Snack: Whole-grain toast with peanut butter + banana; milk or fortified soy milk.
- Lunch: Salmon rice bowl (5–6 oz salmon, 1–1.5 cups cooked rice, mixed veggies, avocado, sesame seeds).
- Pre-workout: Turkey and cheese on whole-grain with spinach + apple.
- Post-workout/Dinner: Lean beef or tofu stir-fry with 1.5–2 cups cooked rice/noodles and mixed vegetables.
- Bed snack: Cottage cheese with kiwi and pumpkin seeds.

High-protein snack list (20–30 g protein options)
- Greek yogurt; cottage cheese; whey or soy isolate shake; turkey/lean beef sticks; edamame; high-protein milk; canned salmon/tuna (low mercury/skipjack); tofu/tempeh; egg bites.

Vegetarian adjustments
- Combine soy/tofu/tempeh, legumes, dairy/eggs (if lacto-ovo) to hit protein targets.
- Consider a complete protein powder (whey/soy/pea blends) if appetite is low.
- Monitor iron, B12, zinc, and choline; supplement as needed with provider oversight.

GI comfort strategies
- Smaller, frequent meals (4–6/day).
- Choose lower-FODMAP carbs if bloating/gas increases (rice, oats, sourdough, potatoes).
- Keep fluids between meals if fullness is an issue; use ginger, peppermint, or B6 per provider for nausea.
- Add soluble fiber (oats, chia, psyllium) gradually to manage constipation.

Guiding principles
- Frequency: 2–3 cardio sessions/week (20–40 minutes), plus light daily movement.
- Intensity: Moderate (RPE 5–7, conversational pace). Avoid high-impact intervals or all-out efforts.
- Modalities: Low-impact, stable options—incline walking, stationary bike (upright or recumbent), elliptical, rowing (short stroke, moderate intensity), swimming or deep-water running. Keep options that feel best as pregnancy progresses.
- Monitoring: Stop/modify if dizziness, chest pain, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, unusual shortness of breath, calf pain/swelling, or pelvic girdle pain. Avoid overheating; train in cool environment, hydrate, consider a fan.
- Pelvic floor: If heaviness/pressure/leakage occurs, reduce intensity/duration, choose more supported modes (bike/elliptical/swim), and add recovery/rest days.

Weekly structure (12 weeks)
- Strength days: Keep cardio easy (Zone 2) or very short flush rides/walks.
- Non-lifting day: Longer steady-state or low-impact intervals.
- Optional: Short walks most days (10–20 min) for circulation and glycemic control.

Heart-rate guidance (optional if she uses a monitor)
- Aim for 60–75% of estimated max HR or talk test. If using 220–age is inaccurate, rely on RPE/talk test.

Warm-up and cool-down template (each cardio session)
- 5–7 min easy ramp-up (RPE 3–4) + dynamic mobility (ankle pumps, hip circles, gentle thoracic rotations).
- Cool-down 3–5 min easy + 2–3 pelvic floor relaxation breaths.

12-week cardio plan by phase
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Build consistency and base
- Session A (Steady Zone 2)
  - Choose: incline treadmill walk, bike, or elliptical
  - 25–30 min @ RPE 5–6; maintain conversational pace
- Session B (Mixed steady + strides)
  - 5–10 min easy
  - 3–5 x 2 min at RPE 6–7 with 2 min easy spin/walk between
  - 5 min easy to finish (total 25–30 min)
- Optional Session C (Flush/recovery on rest day or after lifting)
  - 15–20 min very easy bike or walk @ RPE 4–5

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Maintain aerobic capacity; gentle progression
- Session A (Extended steady)
  - 30–35 min @ RPE 5–6 on preferred modality
- Session B (Low-impact tempo waves)
  - 8 min easy
  - 3–4 x 4 min @ RPE 6–7 with 2–3 min easy between
  - 5 min easy (total 30–35 min)
- Optional Session C (Uphill walk or spin flush)
  - 15–20 min @ RPE 4–5 with light nasal breathing emphasis

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Comfort-first, maintain volume, reduce impact if needed
- Session A (Steady maintenance)
  - 25–30 min @ RPE 5–6; consider bike, recumbent bike, or swimming if walking becomes uncomfortable
- Session B (Mini intervals or cadence play)
  - 6–8 min easy
  - 6–8 x 1 min @ RPE 6–7 with 1–2 min easy between
  - 5 min easy (total 25–30 min)
- Optional Session C (Recovery circulation)
  - 10–15 min very easy + mobility

Weekly placement with strength plan
- Mon (Lower strength): Optional 10–15 min easy spin/walk post-lift
- Wed (Upper strength): Session B (intervals) or A (steady), separate from lifting by ≥6 hours if possible
- Fri (Full-body strength): Optional 10–15 min easy spin/walk post-lift
- Sat/Sun: Session A (longer steady) on the non-lifting day; Optional Session C if feeling good

Modalities and adjustments
- Treadmill walking: 0–6% incline; adjust speed to keep RPE in range. Reduce incline if pelvic girdle pain or calf tightness emerges.
- Stationary/recumbent bike: Great as belly grows; keep knee/hip angles comfortable; avoid excessive forward lean if it increases reflux.
- Elliptical: Low-impact whole-body option; shorten stride if hips/pelvis feel lax.
- Rowing: Use moderate stroke rate and shorter ROM as bump grows; stop if coning, pelvic pressure, or discomfort.
- Swimming/deep-water running: Excellent late-pregnancy choice; cool and buoyant. Avoid flip turns if they cause dizziness.

Pelvic floor-friendly interval ideas (swap in anytime)
- Bike: 8–10 x 60 seconds at RPE 6–7, 60–90 seconds easy
- Elliptical: 5 x 3 minutes RPE 6 with 2 minutes easy
- Pool: 10–12 x 30 seconds hard pull-buoy kick with 60 seconds easy

Recovery, hydration, and fueling for cardio
- Pre: 20–40 g carbs + 10–20 g protein 1–2 hours before; add 300–600 mg sodium if training in heat or if a salty sweater.
- During: Water as thirst guides; for >40 min or in heat, sip electrolytes and consider 15–30 g carbs.
- Post: 25–35 g protein + 40–70 g carbs within 1–2 hours.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.0 L/day baseline + 500–750 ml per training hour; use a fan and breathable clothing.

Progression and autoregulation
- Progress by time first (add 2–5 minutes/session each week if RPE allows), then by adding an interval, not by pushing intensity.
- If RPE >7, HR spikes unusually, or recovery lags, cut the session by 20–30% or switch to lower-impact modality.
- If pelvic girdle pain appears, favor bike/recumbent/swim, shorten stride, reduce incline, and decrease intervals.

Daily movement targets
- Aim 6,000–9,000 steps/day as comfortable, splitting into short walks (5–15 minutes) after meals to aid glucose control and reduce swelling; adjust based on fatigue and swelling.

This cardio plan preserves and supports aerobic fitness, complements her strength work, and adapts as pregnancy progresses, with clear session structures and built-in flexibility.

Global structure and guardrails

- Movement positions: Prioritize standing, seated, side-lying, incline (20–45°), half/tall-kneeling. No flat supine.
- Bracing/breathing: 360° inhale, gentle brace, exhale on exertion; no breath holding.
- Red flags to stop/modify: dizziness, chest pain, vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage, painful contractions, unusual SOB, calf pain/swelling, pronounced pelvic pain/pressure, or midline coning.
